# US-03 — Summary and payment · Spec

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Story | [story.md](story.md) (verbatim, not edited) |
| Status | Approved |
| Version | 0.1 |
| Author | spec-writer subagent (Claude Opus 5.5) |
| Approved by | v0.1: Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21 (HC1 round 1) |
| Related ADRs | [ADR-0001](../../adr/0001-multi-country-content-strategy.md) (`terms` per country with a required `country` relation; `/:country/resumen`; implementation note: summary route and `summaryStepGuard` registered by US-02), [ADR-0002](../../adr/0002-strapi-access-and-security.md) as amended by [ADR-0005](../../adr/0005-e2e-token-scope-for-relations.md) (public `find` on terms, proxy `/api/terms`, published-only reads, e2e token scope), [ADR-0003](../../adr/0003-wizard-state-persistence.md) (clear on successful payment, keep on rejected payment, terms and payment data never stored), [ADR-0006](../../adr/0006-strapi-physical-model-adjustments.md) (typed attributes, `localeTag`), [ADR-0007](../../adr/0007-simulated-price-rule.md) (`calculateFinalPrice` reused). **Needed:** simulated payment design (US-03-Q-01); terms rich-text format and safe rendering (US-03-Q-02). See §10. |

Sources cited in this spec:

- **Story**: [story.md](story.md).
- **Assessment**: requirements quoted verbatim from the assessment PDF by the orchestrator (not in
  the repository).
- **US-01**: [specs/US-01/spec.md](../US-01/spec.md) v0.5 (Approved): the typed step 1 output and
  reserved keys (§7.3), code-owned copy (§8.1), seed values ([seed-fields.md](../US-01/seed-fields.md)).
- **US-02**: [specs/US-02/spec.md](../US-02/spec.md) v0.1 (Approved): the stored `plan: { key }`,
  the offered plans, price display and formatting (BR-03), what it handed to US-03 (§7.4), and the
  summary route and guard (US-02-Q-03, US-02-AC-15).
- **ADR-0001..0007**: accepted ADRs (precedence level 2), with the implementation notes in
  [adr/README.md](../../adr/README.md).
- **Reviews** of US-01 (R1..R4) and US-02 (R1, R2): lessons for a new content type (published-only
  router config, anonymous variants in the draft checks, no bespoke backend code where the schema
  suffices) and the `review-checklist` items on rich text, masking and the disabled pay button.

## 1. Summary

Step 3 of the quote wizard. After choosing a plan, a person in Colombia or Chile sees a summary
of their data, their vehicle's data and the chosen plan with its final price; the document number
is partially masked. From the summary they can go back to edit their data or change the plan.
They read the terms and conditions configured in Strapi for their country, accept them, and pay.
Payment is simulated: no real gateway, no card data. While the simulated payment runs, the pay
button is locked so it cannot be submitted twice. On success the stored quote is cleared and a
confirmation with a simulated quote number is shown; on rejection a clear message is shown and the
person can try again with all their information intact. The same build serves both countries.

## 2. Scope

**In scope**

- The summary page attached to the existing route `/:country/resumen`, behind the existing
  `summaryStepGuard`, without changing the address or the guard (ADR-0001 implementation note).
- Showing step 1 values with their Strapi labels, the chosen plan and its final price (reusing
  `calculateFinalPrice`, ADR-0007, and the US-02 money formatter); masking the document number.
- "Editar mis datos" and "Cambiar plan" back to steps 1 and 2.
- A per-country terms content type in Strapi (ADR-0001), its seed for CO and CL
  ([seed-terms.md](seed-terms.md)), public read access (ADR-0002 anticipates `find` and
  `/api/terms`), safe rendering of its formatted text.
- Accepting the terms, the pay button state, the simulated payment (success and rejection), double
  submit prevention, the simulated quote number, the confirmation, and clearing the wizard state on
  success (ADR-0003).
- Loading, error, retry and "not available" states of the terms.
- Keyboard-only use, accessible names, focus management, mobile and desktop layouts.
- Completing the assessment's full-flow e2e `frontend/e2e/us-01-03-full-flow-co.spec.ts` with the
  summary, terms, payment and confirmation.

**Out of scope**

- Real payment gateways, card or bank data of any kind, real charges ("Payment is simulated: a
  button that leads to a confirmation screen or a mock gateway. Do not integrate real payment
  gateways or use real card data.", Assessment).
- Issuing a policy, sending e-mails, PDFs or receipts, storing quotes on a server ("a database is
  not required", Assessment).
- Versioning of the terms or recording which version was accepted (US-03-Q-12).
- Requiring the person to scroll to the end of the terms before accepting (US-03-Q-12).
- Editing data inline on the summary; returning from step 1 straight to the summary (US-03-Q-11).
- Masking any value other than the document number; reformatting typed values (plates, RUT).
- Payment instalments, discounts, taxes.

## 3. Glossary

Terms defined in the US-01 and US-02 glossaries (country context, published, wizard state, typed
step 1 output, reserved key, offered plan, plan key, final price, today, editor) keep their meaning.

| Term | Meaning in this project |
|---|---|
| Summary | Step 3 of the wizard at `/:country/resumen`: the person's data, the chosen plan, the terms and the pay action. |
| Terms | The terms and conditions of one country: one published Strapi document of the terms content type (§7.1). |
| Accepting the terms | Checking the code-owned checkbox "Acepto los términos y condiciones". Held in the page's memory only (US-03-Q-10). |
| Masked document number | The display form of the reserved `documentNumber` value defined in BR-02. Computed at display time; never stored (ADR-0003). |
| Simulated payment | A front-end-only stand-in for a payment gateway, with a deterministic outcome and no card data (BR-08, US-03-Q-01). |
| Payment attempt | One activation of "Pagar" that the simulated payment accepts, from the start of processing to its outcome. |
| Quote number | The simulated identifier shown on the confirmation (US-03-Q-07). Not stored and not sent anywhere. |
| Confirmation | What the person sees after a successful payment (US-03-Q-06, US-03-Q-13). |

## 4. Business rules

| ID | Original (source) | Refined (precise, testable) | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|
| US-03-BR-01 | Story: "The summary shows the policyholder's data, the vehicle's data and the chosen plan with its final price." | The summary shows, from the typed step 1 output re-derived on entry (US-02-Q-17) and the field configuration of this page load: one row per configured field that has a non-empty value, except `checkbox` fields, with the field's Strapi `label` and its display value (US-03-Q-05). Rows are grouped under "Tu vehículo" (reserved keys `plate`, `make`, `model`, `vehicleYear`) and "Tus datos" (every other key), each in `sortOrder`; a group with no rows is not shown. Display values: `select` → the option's Strapi label; `date` → long Spanish date from the country's `locale` ("15 de mayo de 1990"); `number` → digits with no grouping ("2022"); `text` → as entered (trimmed), except `documentNumber` (BR-02). The chosen plan (`plan.key`) is shown with its name, short description and final price `calculateFinalPrice(basePrice, step 1 output, today)` (ADR-0007), formatted as in US-02-BR-03 with the caption "Precio anual" (US-03-Q-14). | US-03-AC-01, US-03-AC-06 |
| US-03-BR-02 | Story: "The document number is shown partially masked." | The value of the reserved key `documentNumber` is shown masked (US-03-Q-04): let *n* be the number of letters and digits in the value; the last *k* = min(4, ⌊n/2⌋) letters and digits stay visible, every earlier letter or digit becomes "•" (U+2022), and every other character (dots, dashes, spaces) stays in place. The same function applies to every country (no country branch). The full number never appears in the DOM, the document title, the URL or a log on the summary or confirmation. The rule applies only to `documentNumber`. | US-03-AC-05 |
| US-03-BR-03 | Story: "From the summary the person can go back to edit their data or change the plan." | "Editar mis datos" navigates to `/<country>/datos` and "Cambiar plan" to `/<country>/planes`, each as a new history entry. Step 1 values and the chosen plan are kept (ADR-0003, US-02-BR-07). The person returns to the summary through the normal flow (step 1 "Continuar" → step 2 → "Continuar"); the price is recomputed. Leaving the summary discards the terms acceptance and the payment simulation choice (US-03-Q-10, Q-11). Both actions are unavailable during a payment attempt (BR-05). | US-03-AC-07 |
| US-03-BR-04 | Story: "The pay button is enabled only after accepting the terms and conditions." | "Pagar" is enabled if and only if the terms of the country are shown (loaded and well-formed) **and** "Acepto los términos y condiciones" is checked **and** no payment attempt is in progress. Otherwise it is perceivably disabled (`aria-disabled="true"`, stays focusable), activating it does nothing, and the reason is shown next to it and linked to it (US-03-Q-17). Unchecking disables it again. | US-03-AC-02, US-03-AC-08, US-03-AC-12 |
| US-03-BR-05 | Story: "The payment cannot be submitted twice." | One activation of an enabled "Pagar" starts exactly one payment attempt. From that moment until the outcome, "Pagar" is disabled and reads "Procesando pago…", the terms checkbox, the simulation choice, "Editar mis datos" and "Cambiar plan" are unavailable, and further activations (click, Enter, Space, repeated quickly) start no other attempt. After a success no further attempt is possible; after a rejection a new attempt is possible (BR-08). | US-03-AC-03, US-03-AC-09 |
| US-03-BR-06 | Story: "On successful payment, a confirmation with a simulated quote number is shown." | On a successful attempt the wizard state is deleted (the `quote-wizard` entry and the store's in-memory state; ADR-0003: "Entry deleted before the confirmation is shown") and then the confirmation is shown with a quote number of the format `COT-<country code>-<YYYYMMDD of today>-<6 digits>` (US-03-Q-07), kept in memory only. After that, a reload or the browser back action leads to an empty step 1 of the same country through the existing guards. | US-03-AC-03, US-03-AC-10, US-03-AC-11 |
| US-03-BR-07 | Story context: "accept the terms and conditions, whose text varies by country and is managed by the business team from Strapi." | The summary shows the terms of the current country: the published terms documents related to that country, the most recently published one if there are several, skipping malformed ones (US-03-Q-12). Draft-only terms and terms of other countries are never shown, and no anonymous caller can read drafts (ADR-0002). Publishing a change is reflected on the next full page load with no code change. The text keeps its formatting (headings, paragraphs, lists, bold, italic) and is rendered without executing anything an editor typed (US-03-Q-02). No terms text exists in front-end code. | US-03-AC-02, US-03-AC-12, US-03-AC-13, US-03-AC-14, US-03-AC-19 |
| US-03-BR-08 | Story context: "Payment is simulated for this test." Story scenario "Rejected payment". Assessment: "Payment is simulated: a button that leads to a confirmation screen or a mock gateway. Do not integrate real payment gateways or use real card data." | The payment runs entirely in the browser, sends no request and asks for no card, bank or personal data. Its outcome is deterministic and selectable (proposed: a visible "Simulación de pago" choice, US-03-Q-01, ADR needed); processing takes a fixed simulated time (proposed 1.5 s). A rejected attempt shows a clear message, clears nothing (ADR-0003: "Rejected payment: Nothing cleared"), keeps the terms accepted and the simulation choice, and lets the person retry. | US-03-AC-04, US-03-AC-15, US-03-AC-19 |

## 5. Acceptance criteria

Conventions for every scenario:

- "I completed step 1 in Colombia" means the values of US-01-AC-04; "in Chile" means the values in
  the US-02 spec §5 conventions (RUT "12.345.678-5", Nombre completo "Ana Prueba Ficticia", Fecha
  de nacimiento 1990-05-15, Ciudad "Santiago", Patente "BCDF12", Marca "Kia", Modelo "Rio 5",
  Año 2022, consent checked). All values are fictitious seed values.
- "I chose a plan" means "Plan Total" in Colombia and "Plan Protegido" in Chile, then "Continuar"
  on step 2. Today is pinned to **2026-11-21** (final prices $2.310.000 and $528.000, US-02-AC-07).
- Terms are the seed of [seed-terms.md](seed-terms.md).
- "The simulated payment fails / succeeds" means the outcome of the simulated payment is set to
  rejected / approved. With the proposed default of US-03-Q-01 that is the "Simulación de pago"
  choice "Pago rechazado" / "Pago aprobado"; if the ADR decides another mechanism, only this
  convention changes.
- Prices are compared with whitespace removed (US-02-BR-03). Code-owned copy is in §8.1.

### US-03-AC-01 — Complete summary

```gherkin
Scenario Outline: Complete summary
  Given I completed step 1 in <country> and I chose a plan
  When I reach the summary
  Then the address is "/<code>/resumen" and I see the heading "Resumen de tu cotización"
  And under "Tus datos" I see, in this order: <holder rows>
  And under "Tu vehículo" I see, in this order: <vehicle rows>
  And under "Plan elegido" I see "<plan>", its short description and "<price>" with "Precio anual"

  Examples:
    | country  | code | holder rows | vehicle rows | plan | price |
    | Colombia | co | "Tipo de documento" "Cédula de ciudadanía"; "Número de documento" "••••••5678"; "Nombre completo" "Ana Prueba Ficticia"; "Fecha de nacimiento" "15 de mayo de 1990"; "Ciudad" "Medellín" | "Placa" "ABC123"; "Marca" "Mazda"; "Línea" "3 Touring"; "Modelo (año)" "2022" | Plan Total | $2.310.000 |
    | Chile    | cl | "RUT" "••.•••.678-5"; "Nombre completo" "Ana Prueba Ficticia"; "Fecha de nacimiento" "15 de mayo de 1990"; "Ciudad" "Santiago" | "Patente" "BCDF12"; "Marca" "Kia"; "Modelo" "Rio 5"; "Año" "2022" | Plan Protegido | $528.000 |
```

The consent checkbox is not listed (BR-01). The price equals the one shown on step 2 for the same
data and day (ADR-0007).

### US-03-AC-02 — Terms by country

```gherkin
Scenario Outline: Terms by country
  Given I am on the summary in <country>
  When I view the terms and conditions
  Then I see the title "<title>" and the heading "<heading>" of the <country> terms in Strapi
  And I do not see "<other heading>"
  And the pay button is disabled until I accept them

  Examples:
    | country  | title                                                    | heading                 | other heading           |
    | Colombia | Términos y condiciones del seguro de auto – Colombia     | Condiciones principales | Condiciones generales   |

## 7. Content contract (what Strapi must provide)

Logical model below; the physical model follows ADR-0001 (required `manyToOne` `country` relation,
`strictRelations: true` already set), ADR-0006 (typed attributes, no free JSON) and the
`strapi-content-modeling` conventions. Names subject to US-03-Q-03.

### 7.1 Terms collection type (per country, draft & publish on)

| Attribute | Strapi type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | string, required, `maxLength: 150` | Spanish, non-blank. Shown as the terms heading and the region's accessible name. |
| `body` | per the ADR of US-03-Q-02 (proposed: `blocks`), required | Spanish formatted text. |
| `country` | required `manyToOne` relation to `country` | ADR-0001; publishing without it is rejected (`strictRelations`). |

No `key`, `sortOrder`, `isActive` or `version`: unpublishing is how an editor withdraws terms, and
the most recently published one wins (US-03-Q-12). No bespoke backend code (no uniqueness
middleware).

### 7.2 Wire shape and mapping

Request (one per summary entry and per "Reintentar", through the proxy, published only, 10 s
timeout):

```
GET /api/terms?filters[country][code][$eq]=CO&fields[0]=title&fields[1]=body
  &fields[2]=publishedAt&sort[0]=publishedAt:desc&pagination[pageSize]=10
```

Mapping wire → logical `Terms` (boundary parser):

| Wire attribute | Valid when | Logical attribute |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | non-blank string | `title` |
| `body` | per the ADR of US-03-Q-02; with `blocks`: an array whose supported nodes yield at least one non-blank text | `blocks` (the whitelisted, typed node tree) |
| `publishedAt` | ISO date-time string | used for ordering only |

The parser sorts by `publishedAt` descending itself and does not rely on the server sort. A
malformed entry is skipped with a `console.warn` naming the problem, never the text.

### 7.3 Seed (summary)

Full text in the annex [seed-terms.md](seed-terms.md). Idempotent, natural key country code +
`title`.

| Country | Published | Draft only |
|---|---|---|
| CO | "Términos y condiciones del seguro de auto – Colombia" (5 blocks, bulleted list, heading "Condiciones principales") | "Términos y condiciones (borrador)" |
| CL | "Términos y condiciones del seguro automotriz – Chile" (5 blocks, numbered list, heading "Condiciones generales") | — |

### 7.4 Access (ADR-0002, ADR-0005)

- Public role: add exactly the terms `find` (`api::term.term.find` with the US-03-Q-03 default),
  reconciled in bootstrap; no `findOne`. Justification: the summary must show the country's terms
  (BR-07); data exposed: published terms text, public by nature.
- Router: `createCoreRouter(<terms uid>, publishedOnlyConfig())` with a fresh config object
  (US-01-R2-F03).
- Proxy: add `/api/terms` to the GET-only allow-list.
- E2E write token for AC-14 (ADR-0005 general rule): exactly terms `create`, terms `delete` and
  `api::country.country.find`; created and deleted in the Playwright Node process only.

### 7.5 What US-03 reads from the wizard state and the page load

- From the `quote-wizard` entry (ADR-0003): the raw step 1 values (re-derived into the typed
  output with this page load's field configuration, US-02-Q-17) and `plan.key`. US-03 adds
  **nothing** to the entry: no terms acceptance, simulation choice, payment data or quote number.
- From this page load's content: field configuration (labels, option labels, types, `sortOrder`),
  the offered plans (name, short description, `basePrice`), the country (`code`, `currencyCode`,
  `locale`) and the terms.
- On success, the whole entry is deleted and the store's in-memory step 1 values and plan are
  reset (BR-06).

## 8. UI states

| State | Trigger | What the user sees | Accessibility notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Arrival | Navigation to the summary (guard passed) | Heading "Resumen de tu cotización", "Tus datos", "Tu vehículo", "Plan elegido", the edit buttons, the terms section, the simulation group, "Pagar" (disabled) | Focus on the `h1`; document title per §8.1 |
| Terms loading | Terms request in flight | "Cargando términos y condiciones…" in the terms section; no checkbox | Section `aria-busy="true"`; polite live region |
| Terms error | Timeout (10 s), network or HTTP error, unexpected response shape | "No pudimos cargar los términos y condiciones. Intenta de nuevo.", "Reintentar" | `role="alert"`; focus stays on the heading (the error is not caused by the user); "Reintentar" reachable by Tab |
| Terms not available | Zero well-formed published terms | "Los términos y condiciones no están disponibles en este momento. No es posible pagar." | Polite live region |
| Terms shown, not accepted | Terms loaded | Terms title and text in a scrollable region, unchecked checkbox, hint "Acepta los términos y condiciones para pagar.", "Pagar" `aria-disabled` | Region `tabindex="0"`, named by the title; hint in `aria-describedby` of "Pagar" |
| Ready to pay | Checkbox checked | "Pagar" enabled; hint hidden | — |
| Processing | "Pagar" activated | "Procesando pago…" on the button; every action unavailable | Page `aria-busy="true"`; status announced once |
| Rejected | Simulated payment rejected | AC-04 message next to "Pagar"; everything kept and enabled again | `role="alert"`; focus stays on "Pagar" |
| Confirmation | Simulated payment succeeded | "Pago confirmado", quote number, simulation notice, "Nueva cotización" | Focus on the confirmation `h1`; document title per §8.1 |

### 8.1 Code-owned copy added by US-03

Spanish, the same for both countries, in front-end code; extends US-01 §8.1 and US-02 §8.1.
"Reintentar" and "Precio anual" already exist.

| String | Where |
|---|---|
| "Resumen de tu cotización" | Summary heading |
| "Resumen de tu cotización \| Cotizador de seguro de auto" | Summary document title |
| "Tus datos" / "Tu vehículo" / "Plan elegido" / "Términos y condiciones" | Section headings |
| "Editar mis datos" / "Cambiar plan" | Back actions |
| "Número oculto, termina en {tail}" / "Número oculto" | Accessible text of the masked document number |
| "Cargando términos y condiciones…" | Terms loading |
| "No pudimos cargar los términos y condiciones. Intenta de nuevo." | Terms error |
| "Los términos y condiciones no están disponibles en este momento. No es posible pagar." | No terms |
| "Acepto los términos y condiciones" | Terms checkbox label |
| "Acepta los términos y condiciones para pagar." | Hint of the disabled "Pagar" |
| "Simulación de pago (no se realiza ningún cobro)" / "Pago aprobado" / "Pago rechazado" | Simulation group (subject to US-03-Q-01) |
| "Pagar" / "Procesando pago…" | Pay button and its processing label |
| "El pago fue rechazado y no se realizó ningún cobro. Puedes intentarlo de nuevo." | Rejected payment |
| "Pago confirmado" | Confirmation heading |
| "Pago confirmado \| Cotizador de seguro de auto" | Confirmation document title |
| "Tu número de cotización es" | Before the quote number |
| "Este es un pago simulado; no se realizó ningún cobro real." | Confirmation notice |
| "Nueva cotización" | Confirmation action |

## 9. Non-functional requirements

- **Accessibility (Assessment: "The wizard can be completed using only the keyboard, and fields
  have accessible labels"):** focus on the heading on arrival and on confirmation, description
  lists for data, a named focusable terms region, a labelled checkbox, a named radio group, a
  perceivable disabled "Pagar" with its reason, alerts announced once (AC-16, AC-17). WCAG 2.2 AA;
  screen reader pass at HC3.
- **Responsive (Assessment: "Works on mobile and desktop"):** 320–1440 CSS px without horizontal
  scroll; one column on narrow screens; targets ≥ 24 × 24 CSS px (AC-18, manual).
- **Multi-country (Assessment: "The same application and the same build serve Colombia and
  Chile"):** no terms text, field label, plan, currency, date format or masking branch per country
  in front-end code; dates and prices use the country's `locale` and `currencyCode` from Strapi.
- **Security / privacy (Assessment: "No Strapi token with write permissions may reach the
  browser. Public role permissions minimal and justified"; "Use fictitious data only."):** one
  added public permission (§7.4); reads through the GET-only proxy; drafts never anonymous; no
  request during payment; no card data; masking at display time; no value, quote number or terms
  text in logs; rich text rendered without executing editor input (AC-13, AC-19). Seed and test
  data fictitious.
- **Persistence (Assessment: "Use a front-end strategy to persist the data; a database is not
  required."):** ADR-0003 unchanged; US-03 adds nothing to storage and deletes the entry on success.
- **Performance:** one terms request per summary entry; summary data comes from content already
  loaded by the guards in this page load; the price rule and masking are synchronous pure functions.
- **Testing (Assessment: "Unit tests for the relevant logic and at least one e2e test of the full
  flow for one country"):** masking, value display, quote number, terms parser and the simulated
  payment are unit tested; the CO full-flow e2e is completed end to end (US-03-Q-16).
- **Language:** end-user copy Spanish; code, logs and docs English.

## 10. ADRs

- **Referenced (accepted, binding):**
  1. ADR-0001 — terms content type with a required `manyToOne` `country`; `strictRelations`;
     `/:country/resumen` with `summaryStepGuard` (implementation note: built by US-02, US-03
     attaches the page only); focus on the arriving step's heading. Used by: BR-07, §7.1, AC-16.
  2. ADR-0002 (amended by ADR-0005) — terms `find` on the public role and `/api/terms` on the
     proxy (both anticipated for US-03), `publishedOnlyConfig()`, `no-store`; e2e token with `find`
     on relation targets. Used by: BR-07, §7.4, AC-14, AC-19.
  3. ADR-0003 — entry deleted before the confirmation on success; nothing cleared on rejection;
     terms and payment data never stored; masking at display time. Used by: BR-02, BR-06, BR-08,
     AC-04, AC-11.
  4. ADR-0006 — typed attributes, no free JSON (relevant to the terms `body` format). Used by: §7.1.
  5. ADR-0007 — `calculateFinalPrice` in `frontend/src/app/shared/price-rules.ts`, imported, not
     copied, with the same `CLOCK`. Used by: BR-01, AC-01, AC-07.
  6. ADR-0004 applies to the step 1 form only; the summary's checkbox and radio group are plain
     controls, not a Strapi-driven form.
- **Needed (for the architect):**
  1. **Simulated payment design** (US-03-Q-01): where the outcome comes from (visible simulation
     choice, mock gateway page, fictitious test cards, hidden trigger), processing time and its
     injection for tests, the service boundary a real gateway would replace, no request and no
     card data. Proposed default in US-03-Q-01.
  2. **Terms rich-text format and safe rendering** (US-03-Q-02): `blocks` with a whitelist
     renderer vs Markdown `richtext` with a parser and sanitised `[innerHTML]` vs plain `text`;
     dependency impact; how unsupported nodes degrade. Proposed default in US-03-Q-02.
- **Implementation notes (no new decision), if the defaults are accepted:** the terms permission
  name `api::term.term.find` on ADR-0002 (US-03-Q-03). Only if US-03-Q-06 takes the alternative:
  a confirmation route on ADR-0001.

## 11. Test mapping

Planned locations follow CLAUDE.md §6; the test-engineer may adjust unit and component paths.
Short names: `document-mask.spec.ts` = `frontend/src/app/shared/document-mask.spec.ts`;
`summary-rows.spec.ts` = `frontend/src/app/shared/summary-rows.spec.ts` (rows, groups, display

`terms.spec.ts` = `frontend/src/app/shared/terms.spec.ts` (boundary parser and selection);
`terms-api.spec.ts` = `frontend/src/app/core/terms-api.spec.ts`;
`rich-text.spec.ts` = `frontend/src/app/shared/rich-text.spec.ts` (renderer component);
`payment.spec.ts` = the simulated payment service test (name per the ADR of US-03-Q-01);
`quote-store-clear.spec.ts` = `frontend/src/app/core/quote-store-clear.spec.ts`;
`summary-page.spec.ts` = `frontend/src/app/features/summary/summary-page.spec.ts`;
`full-flow-co` = `frontend/e2e/us-01-03-full-flow-co.spec.ts`;
`summary-payment-cl` = `frontend/e2e/us-03-summary-payment-cl.spec.ts` (proposed, US-03-Q-16).

You are the **test-engineer** of this project's agentic flow (see `FLOW.md`, step 3).

## Responsibility

Turn every acceptance criterion of an **approved** spec into an automated test, before the
implementation exists, so that "done" means "the spec's tests pass".

## Inputs

- `specs/US-XX/spec.md` with status `Approved`. **If the spec is not approved, stop and report.**
- The accepted ADRs it references, and `CLAUDE.md`.
- The skills `test-from-spec` and `dynamic-form-fields`. For Angular testing patterns, use
  `.claude/skills/angular-developer/references/testing-fundamentals.md` as reference.

## Outputs

- Unit and component tests (`*.spec.ts` next to the planned source files, using the planned
  names from the spec or tasks).
- E2E tests in `frontend/e2e/`.
- Shared test helpers in `frontend/src/testing/`.
- A `tasks.md` update: the test files per task, and the current step.

Write access is enforced by a hook: test files and `tasks.md` only. You cannot edit production
code or the spec.

- Derive the assertions from the spec, not from existing implementation code.

28	## 1. Summary
29	
30	Step 3 of the quote wizard. After choosing a plan, a person in Colombia or Chile sees a summary
31	of their data, their vehicle's data and the chosen plan with its final price; the document number
32	is partially masked. From the summary they can go back to edit their data or change the plan.
33	They read the terms and conditions configured in Strapi for their country, accept them, and pay.
34	Payment is simulated: no real gateway, no card data. While the simulated payment runs, the pay
35	button is locked so it cannot be submitted twice. On success the stored quote is cleared and a
36	confirmation with a simulated quote number is shown; on rejection a clear message is shown and the
37	person can try again with all their information intact. The same build serves both countries.
38	
39	## 2. Scope
40	
41	**In scope**
42	
43	- The summary page attached to the existing route `/:country/resumen`, behind the existing
44	  `summaryStepGuard`, without changing the address or the guard (ADR-0001 implementation note).
45	- Showing step 1 values with their Strapi labels, the chosen plan and its final price (reusing
46	  `calculateFinalPrice`, ADR-0007, and the US-02 money formatter); masking the document number.
47	- "Editar mis datos" and "Cambiar plan" back to steps 1 and 2.
48	- A per-country terms content type in Strapi (ADR-0001), its seed for CO and CL
49	  ([seed-terms.md](seed-terms.md)), public read access (ADR-0002 anticipates `find` and
50	  `/api/terms`), safe rendering of its formatted text.
51	- Accepting the terms, the pay button state, the simulated payment (success and rejection), double
52	  submit prevention, the simulated quote number, the confirmation, and clearing the wizard state on
53	  success (ADR-0003).
54	- Loading, error, retry and "not available" states of the terms.
55	- Keyboard-only use, accessible names, focus management, mobile and desktop layouts.
56	- Completing the assessment's full-flow e2e `frontend/e2e/us-01-03-full-flow-co.spec.ts` with the
57	  summary, terms, payment and confirmation.
58	
59	**Out of scope**
60	
61	- Real payment gateways, card or bank data of any kind, real charges ("Payment is simulated: a
62	  button that leads to a confirmation screen or a mock gateway. Do not integrate real payment
63	  gateways or use real card data.", Assessment).
64	- Issuing a policy, sending e-mails, PDFs or receipts, storing quotes on a server ("a database is
65	  not required", Assessment).
66	- Versioning of the terms or recording which version was accepted (US-03-Q-12).
67	- Requiring the person to scroll to the end of the terms before accepting (US-03-Q-12).
68	- Editing data inline on the summary; returning from step 1 straight to the summary (US-03-Q-11).
69	- Masking any value other than the document number; reformatting typed values (plates, RUT).
70	- Payment instalments, discounts, taxes.
71	
72	## 3. Glossary
73	
74	Terms defined in the US-01 and US-02 glossaries (country context, published, wizard state, typed
75	step 1 output, reserved key, offered plan, plan key, final price, today, editor) keep their meaning.
76	
77	| Term | Meaning in this project |
78	|---|---|
79	| Summary | Step 3 of the wizard at `/:country/resumen`: the person's data, the chosen plan, the terms and the pay action. |
80	| Terms | The terms and conditions of one country: one published Strapi document of the terms content type (§7.1). |
81	| Accepting the terms | Checking the code-owned checkbox "Acepto los términos y condiciones". Held in the page's memory only (US-03-Q-10). |
82	| Masked document number | The display form of the reserved `documentNumber` value defined in BR-02. Computed at display time; never stored (ADR-0003). |
83	| Simulated payment | A front-end-only stand-in for a payment gateway, with a deterministic outcome and no card data (BR-08, US-03-Q-01). |
84	| Payment attempt | One activation of "Pagar" that the simulated payment accepts, from the start of processing to its outcome. |
85	| Quote number | The simulated identifier shown on the confirmation (US-03-Q-07). Not stored and not sent anywhere. |
86	| Confirmation | What the person sees after a successful payment (US-03-Q-06, US-03-Q-13). |
87	
88	## 4. Business rules
89	
90	| ID | Original (source) | Refined (precise, testable) | Covered by |
91	|---|---|---|---|
92	| US-03-BR-01 | Story: "The summary shows the policyholder's data, the vehicle's data and the chosen plan with its final price." | The summary shows, from the typed step 1 output re-derived on entry (US-02-Q-17) and the field configuration of this page load: one row per configured field that has a non-empty value, except `checkbox` fields, with the field's Strapi `label` and its display value (US-03-Q-05). Rows are grouped under "Tu vehículo" (reserved keys `plate`, `make`, `model`, `vehicleYear`) and "Tus datos" (every other key), each in `sortOrder`; a group with no rows is not shown. Display values: `select` → the option's Strapi label; `date` → long Spanish date from the country's `locale` ("15 de mayo de 1990"); `number` → digits with no grouping ("2022"); `text` → as entered (trimmed), except `documentNumber` (BR-02). The chosen plan (`plan.key`) is shown with its name, short description and final price `calculateFinalPrice(basePrice, step 1 output, today)` (ADR-0007), formatted as in US-02-BR-03 with the caption "Precio anual" (US-03-Q-14). | US-03-AC-01, US-03-AC-06 |
93	| US-03-BR-02 | Story: "The document number is shown partially masked." | The value of the reserved key `documentNumber` is shown masked (US-03-Q-04): let *n* be the number of letters and digits in the value; the last *k* = min(4, ⌊n/2⌋) letters and digits stay visible, every earlier letter or digit becomes "•" (U+2022), and every other character (dots, dashes, spaces) stays in place. The same function applies to every country (no country branch). The full number never appears in the DOM, the document title, the URL or a log on the summary or confirmation. 513	## 7. Content contract (what Strapi must provide)
514	
515	Logical model below; the physical model follows ADR-0001 (required `manyToOne` `country` relation,
516	`strictRelations: true` already set), ADR-0006 (typed attributes, no free JSON) and the
517	`strapi-content-modeling` conventions. Names subject to US-03-Q-03.
518	
519	### 7.1 Terms collection type (per country, draft & publish on)
520	
521	| Attribute | Strapi type | Rules |
522	|---|---|---|
523	| `title` | string, required, `maxLength: 150` | Spanish, non-blank. Shown as the terms heading and the region's accessible name. |
524	| `body` | per the ADR of US-03-Q-02 (proposed: `blocks`), required | Spanish formatted text. |
525	| `country` | required `manyToOne` relation to `country` | ADR-0001; publishing without it is rejected (`strictRelations`). |
526	
527	No `key`, `sortOrder`, `isActive` or `version`: unpublishing is how an editor withdraws terms, and
528	the most recently published one wins (US-03-Q-12). No bespoke backend code (no uniqueness
529	middleware).
530	
531	### 7.2 Wire shape and mapping
532	
533	Request (one per summary entry and per "Reintentar", through the proxy, published only, 10 s
534	timeout):
535	
536	```
537	GET /api/terms?filters[country][code][$eq]=CO&fields[0]=title&fields[1]=body
538	  &fields[2]=publishedAt&sort[0]=publishedAt:desc&pagination[pageSize]=10
539	```
540	
541	Mapping wire → logical `Terms` (boundary parser):
542	
543	| Wire attribute | Valid when | Logical attribute |
544	|---|---|---|
545	| `title` | non-blank string | `title` |
546	| `body` | per the ADR of US-03-Q-02; with `blocks`: an array whose supported nodes yield at least one non-blank text | `blocks` (the whitelisted, typed node tree) |
547	| `publishedAt` | ISO date-time string | used for ordering only |
548	
549	The parser sorts by `publishedAt` descending itself and does not rely on the server sort. A
550	malformed entry is skipped with a `console.warn` naming the problem, never the text.
551

553	
554	Full text in the annex [seed-terms.md](seed-terms.md). Idempotent, natural key country code +
555	`title`.

557	| Country | Published | Draft only |
558	|---|---|---|
559	| CO | "Términos y condiciones del seguro de auto – Colombia" (5 blocks, bulleted list, heading "Condiciones principales") | "Términos y condiciones (borrador)" |
560	| CL | "Términos y condiciones del seguro automotriz – Chile" (5 blocks, numbered list, heading "Condiciones generales") | — |

566	  (BR-07); data exposed: published terms text, public by nature.

569	- Proxy: add `/api/terms` to the GET-only allow-list.

571	  `api::country.country.find`; created and deleted in the Playwright Node process only.

574	
575	- From the `quote-wizard` entry (ADR-0003): the raw step 1 values (re-derived into the typed
576	  output with this page load's field configuration, US-02-Q-17) and `plan.key`. US-03 adds
577	  **nothing** to the entry: no terms acceptance, simulation choice, payment data or quote number.
578	- From this page load's content: field configuration (labels, option labels, types, `sortOrder`),
579	  the offered plans (name, short description, `basePrice`), the country (`code`, `currencyCode`,
580	  `locale`) and the terms.

624	## 9. Non-functional requirements
625	
626	- **Accessibility (Assessment: "The wizard can be completed using only the keyboard, and fields
627	  have accessible labels"):** focus on the heading on arrival and on confirmation, description
628	  lists for data, a named focusable terms region, a labelled checkbox, a named radio group, a
629	  perceivable disabled "Pagar" with its reason, alerts announced once (AC-16, AC-17). WCAG 2.2 AA;
630	  screen reader pass at HC3.
631	- **Responsive (Assessment: "Works on mobile and desktop"):** 320–1440 CSS px without horizontal
632	  scroll; one column on narrow screens; targets ≥ 24 × 24 CSS px (AC-18, manual).
633	- **Multi-country (Assessment: "The same application and the same build serve Colombia and
634	  Chile"):** no terms text, field label, plan, currency, date format or masking branch per country
635	  in front-end code; dates and prices use the country's `locale` and `currencyCode` from Strapi.
636	- **Security / privacy (Assessment: "No Strapi token with write permissions may reach the
637	  browser. Public role permissions minimal and justified"; "Use fictitious data only."):** one
638	  added public permission (§7.4); reads through the GET-only proxy; drafts never anonymous; no
639	  request during payment; no card data; masking at display time; no value, quote number or terms
640	  text in logs; rich text rendered without executing editor input (AC-13, AC-19). Seed and test
641	  data fictitious.
642	- **Persistence (Assessment: "Use a front-end strategy to persist the data; a database is not
643	  required."):** ADR-0003 unchanged; US-03 adds nothing to storage and deletes the entry on success.
644	- **Performance:** one terms request per summary entry; summary data comes from content already
645	  loaded by the guards in this page load; the price rule and masking are synchronous pure functions.
646	- **Testing (Assessment: "Unit tests for the relevant logic and at least one e2e test of the full
647	  flow for one country"):** masking, value display, quote number, terms parser and the simulated
648	  payment are unit tested; the CO full-flow e2e is completed end to end (US-03-Q-16).
649	- **Language:** end-user copy Spanish; code, logs and docs English.

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## easel
Tools registered by the cc-plugin-easel plugin through $.tool.register.

While auto mode is active:

You can do much of your work through the Bash tool when it is the simpler route: read files with cat, head, or sed -n, search with grep and find, and make small, mechanical file changes with sed, heredocs, or short scripts instead of the dedicated Read, Edit, or Write tools. The choice is yours: prefer Edit or Write when a shell edit would be fragile, such as exact or multi-line replacements, or sed/awk flags that differ between GNU and BSD/macOS.

9	# ADR-0008: Simulated payment: a visible outcome choice, a front-end gateway boundary, no card data
10	
11	## Context and Problem Statement
12	
13	US-03 ends the wizard with a payment. The assessment says: "Payment is simulated: a button that
14	leads to a confirmation screen or a mock gateway. Do not integrate real payment gateways or use
15	real card data." The story has a "Rejected payment" scenario ("Given … the simulated payment
16	fails, When I click pay"), and the same build serves users and tests, so the rejected path must be
17	reachable in the production build without a test-only switch. We must decide where the outcome
18	comes from, how long processing takes and how tests control it, which boundary a real gateway
19	would later replace, how double submission is prevented, what the quote number is, what is cleared,
20	how the processing state is announced, and how "no real card data" is guaranteed and checked. The
21	human accepted the spec's proposal at HC1 (US-03-Q-01: "OK", Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21) and asked
22	for it to be weighed against real alternatives. Story: US-03 (`specs/US-03/spec.md` §4 BR-05,
23	BR-06, BR-08; §6 US-03-Q-01).
24	
25	## Decision Drivers
26	
27	- D1. "Payment is simulated … Do not integrate real payment gateways or use real card data."
28	  (source: Assessment; US-03-BR-08).
29	- D2. The rejected path is testable with the same build, end to end, and deterministically
30	  (source: story "Rejected payment"; US-03-AC-04, US-03-BR-08; Assessment: "the same application
31	  and the same build serve Colombia and Chile").
32	- D3. "The payment cannot be submitted twice." (source: story; US-03-BR-05, US-03-AC-09).
33	- D4. Success deletes the wizard state before the confirmation; rejection clears nothing; payment
34	  data is never stored (source: ADR-0003; US-03-BR-06, BR-08, Q-10).
35	- D5. No personal data leaves the browser; reads only, through the GET-only proxy; no write path
36	  for anonymous callers (source: ADR-0002 as amended by ADR-0005; US-03-AC-19).
37	- D6. Keyboard-only use and perceivable states: the disabled pay button explains why, the
38	  processing and rejection states are announced once (source: Assessment, accessibility;
39	  US-03-AC-16, AC-17, Q-17; `review-checklist`: "Disabled pay button: its state is perceivable").
40	- D7. Unit tests control time and randomness; "today" comes from the injectable `CLOCK`
41	  (source: Assessment, testing; US-01-Q-06; ADR-0007 D8; US-03-Q-07).
42	- D8. Smallest change: no new route, guard, dependency or backend code (source: human decisions
43	  recorded as D3 in ADR-0005, D4 in ADR-0006, D12 in ADR-0007; US-03-Q-06 keeps the
44	  confirmation on `/:country/resumen`).
45	- D9. A real gateway can later replace the simulation in one place (source: US-03-Q-01, "It is a
46	  design that a real gateway would later replace").
47	
48	## Considered Options
49	
50	1. **A. Visible outcome choice on the summary**: a code-owned radio group "Simulación de pago (no
51	   se realiza ningún cobro)" with "Pago aprobado" (default) and "Pago rechazado", read when
52	   "Pagar" is activated, passed to a front-end simulated gateway that waits a fixed time and
53	   resolves; no card fields; no request.
54	2. **B. Mock gateway screen**: "Pagar" opens a gateway stand-in (a route such as
55	   `/:country/pago`, or a dialog) that shows the amount and two buttons, "Aprobar pago" and
56	   "Rechazar pago"; the outcome is chosen there.
57	3. **C. Deterministic rule on the input** ("magic values"): the outcome follows from the person's
58	   data, for example a document number or plate ending in a reserved value means "rejected"
59	   (variant: a hidden URL parameter such as `?pago=rechazado`).
60	4. **D. Random outcome**: a fixed share of attempts (for example 20 %) is rejected.
61	5. **E. Fictitious test card form**: card number, expiry and security code fields; reserved test
62	   numbers decide the outcome, as in real gateway sandboxes.
63	
64	**Excluded, because it contradicts accepted ADRs: a backend mock endpoint** (for example
65	`POST /api/payments` in Strapi that answers approved or rejected). ADR-0002 makes the content API
66	read-only for the browser: the proxy forwards only `GET`/`HEAD` on an allow-list and answers `405`
67	to anything else, and the public role holds only `find` permissions. A payment endpoint needs a
68	write-like route open to anonymous callers, a new public permission or custom route, a proxy
69	exception for `POST`, and a request body carrying at least the plan and amount (US-03-AC-19
70	requires that no request contains the plan key or any step 1 value). It would also add bespoke
71	backend code for a simulation (against D8). Choosing it would need an ADR superseding ADR-0002.
72	
73	## Decision Outcome
74	
75	Chosen option: **"A. Visible outcome choice on the summary"**, because it is the only option that
76	is deterministic for both outcomes with the same build and no hidden behaviour (D2), asks for no
77	card data at all (D1), sends no request (D5), needs no new route, guard or dependency (D8), and
78	lets the story's scenario read as written: the outcome is set ("Given … fails") before the
79	activation ("When I click pay"). The gateway boundary (below) is what a real integration would
80	replace (D9).
81	
82	### What is decided
83	
84	**Outcome choice (code-owned copy, spec §8.1)**
85	
86	- A `fieldset` with the `legend` "Simulación de pago (no se realiza ningún cobro)" and two native
87	  radio inputs, "Pago aprobado" (value `approved`, checked on arrival) and "Pago rechazado" (value
88	  `rejected`). Native radios give the radio group role, its accessible name from the legend, and
89	  arrow-key selection (US-03-AC-17).
90	- The choice lives in the page's memory only. It is never written to `sessionStorage`, the URL or
91	  a log (ADR-0003, US-03-Q-10). It is kept after a rejection and reset when the page is left or
92	  reloaded (US-03-BR-03, BR-08).
93	- The value is read **once**, when an attempt starts, and passed to the gateway. The group is
94	  disabled during the attempt, so it cannot change mid-attempt.
95	
96	**Gateway boundary (the part a real gateway replaces, D9)**
97	
98	- `frontend/src/app/core/payment-gateway.ts`: an abstract class `PaymentGateway` used as the DI
99	  token, with
100	  `pay(request: PaymentRequest, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<PaymentResult>`, where
101	  `PaymentRequest = { simulatedOutcome: 'approved' | 'rejected' }` and
102	  `PaymentResult = { status: 'approved' } | { status: 'rejected' }`. No amount, plan, country or
103	  personal value is passed: nothing that is not needed exists at the boundary.
104	- `frontend/src/app/core/simulated-payment-gateway.ts`: `SimulatedPaymentGateway`, provided as
105	  `{ provide: PaymentGateway, useClass: SimulatedPaymentGateway }`. It injects **no** `HttpClient`
106	  and no storage; it waits `SIMULATED_PROCESSING_MS = 1500` through the injected delay, then
107	  resolves to `{ status: request.simulatedOutcome }`. File names follow CLAUDE.md §6 (intent-
108	  revealing, no role suffix); the spec's `payment.spec.ts` is
109	  `simulated-payment-gateway.spec.ts`.
110	- A real gateway would replace `SimulatedPaymentGateway` and `PaymentRequest` (it would carry a
111	  payment token from the provider's own hosted fields, never card data in this app), and remove
112	  the outcome choice. The page's states (processing, rejected, confirmed) stay.
113	
114	**Injectable delay and clock (D7)**
115	
116	- `PAYMENT_DELAY`: `InjectionToken<(ms: number, signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<void>>`, in
117	  `simulated-payment-gateway.ts`, default factory based on `setTimeout` and cleared on abort
118	  (the promise rejects with an `AbortError`). It must be timer-based, never a loop on `Date.now()`:
119	  the e2e tests pin the page clock with `page.clock.setFixedTime`, which (verified, playwright-core
120	  1.65.1 `types/types.d.ts`) "Makes `Date.now` and `new Date()` return fixed fake time at all
121	  times, keeps all the timers running", so a timer completes in 1.5 s while a `Date.now()` loop
122	  would never end.
123	- Unit and component tests either use Vitest fake timers (`vi.useFakeTimers()`,
124	  `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(1500)`, verified in vitest 5.1.1 `dist/index.d.ts`) or provide a
125	  controllable `PAYMENT_DELAY`.
126	- E2E tests keep the real 1.5 s (US-03-AC-15 measures it from the Node side, not with the page's
127	  pinned `Date`). They must not use `page.clock.install()` without `runFor`, because that also
128	  freezes timers.
129	- "Today" for the quote number comes from `CLOCK` (`frontend/src/app/core/clock.ts`,
130	  `InjectionToken<() => Date>`), read when the approved result arrives; the date is the browser's
131	  local date (US-01-Q-06).
132	
133	**Double-submit prevention (D3, US-03-BR-05)**
134	
135	Three layers, each sufficient on its own for its case:
136	
137	1. **Synchronous page guard.** The pay handler is bound to `(click)` only (a native `button`
138	   turns Enter and Space into one `click`; no extra key handlers). It returns at once unless
139	   `canPay()` holds (terms shown, accepted, state `idle` or `rejected`), and it sets the page state
140	   to `processing` **before** any `await`. A second click in the same task finds `processing`.
141	2. **Gateway in-flight flag.** `SimulatedPaymentGateway` holds a private `inFlight` flag; a `pay`
142	   call while it is set starts no timer and rejects with a `PaymentInProgressError` that the page
143	   ignores. This protects any future caller, not only this page.
144	3. **Perceivable lock.** During `processing`: "Pagar" keeps focus and reads "Procesando pago…",
145	   with `aria-disabled="true"` (not native `disabled`: MDN, "disabled controls cannot receive
146	   focus", which would drop the keyboard user's focus to the page body); the outcome `fieldset` and
147	   the terms checkbox are natively disabled; "Editar mis datos" and "Cambiar plan" are
148	   `aria-disabled="true"` and their handlers return early. `aria-disabled` does not block clicks by
149	   itself, so every handler checks the state.
150	
151	After `approved`, the page state is `confirmed` and no handler starts another attempt. After
152	`rejected`, a new attempt is possible.
153	
154	**Leaving during processing**
155	
156	- The page owns an `AbortController`; `DestroyRef.onDestroy` aborts it. Browser back during an
157	  attempt destroys the page, the delay rejects, and **nothing** is cleared or shown (an attempt
158	  never completes on a page that is gone). A reload abandons the attempt the same way (US-03-Q-08).
159	
160	**Simulated quote number (US-03-Q-07, AC-10)**
161	
162	- Format `COT-<country code>-<YYYYMMDD>-<6 digits>`, for example `COT-CO-20261121-482913`.
163	  `COT` stands for *cotización*; the number is fictitious, not unique across sessions (one in a
164	  million per country and day), and the confirmation says the payment is simulated.
165	- `frontend/src/app/shared/quote-number.ts`: a pure `formatQuoteNumber(countryCode, today,
166	  digits)` (upper-case code, local `YYYYMMDD`, `digits` zero-padded to 6).
167	- `frontend/src/app/core/random-digits.ts`: `RANDOM_DIGITS`, `InjectionToken<() => number>`
168	  returning an integer in `[0, 999 999]`. The default uses `crypto.getRandomValues` on a
169	  `Uint32Array(1)` with rejection sampling (discard values ≥ 4 294 000 000, then `% 1 000 000`),
170	  so every value is equally likely. MDN: `getRandomValues()` "is the only member of the `Crypto`
171	  interface which can be used from an insecure context", so it works on the plain-HTTP
172	  `docker compose` stack. Tests provide a fixed source.
173	- The number is kept only in the page's memory: never stored, sent, logged, or put in the URL or
174	  the document title (US-03-AC-10).
175	
176	**What is cleared and kept (ADR-0003, D4)**
177	
178	| Outcome | Wizard state (`quote-wizard` entry and `QuoteStore` memory) | Page memory | Shown |
179	|---|---|---|---|
180	| Approved | **Deleted** through a new `QuoteStore` method (for example `clearQuote()`), which removes the entry and resets the in-memory step 1 values and plan, **before** the confirmation state is set | Quote number kept; terms acceptance and outcome choice discarded with the summary view | Confirmation (US-03-Q-13) |
181	| Rejected | **Nothing** cleared | Terms acceptance and outcome choice kept | Rejection message; "Pagar" enabled again |
182	| Abandoned (back, reload during processing) | Nothing cleared | Lost with the page | Whatever the navigation shows |
183	
184	Order on approval: result → quote number (`CLOCK`, `RANDOM_DIGITS`) → `clearQuote()` → page
185	state `confirmed` → document title "Pago confirmado | Cotizador de seguro de auto" → focus on the
186	"Pago confirmado" heading after render (`afterNextRender`). Only `QuoteStore` touches
187	`sessionStorage` (ADR-0003). The confirmation is rendered by the same component, **not** in a
188	`@defer` block or a lazy chunk, so no request (not even a JavaScript chunk) is sent between the
189	activation and the confirmation (US-03-AC-15).
190	
191	**Accessibility of the processing state (D6, US-03-AC-17)**
192	
193	- The summary content gets `aria-busy="true"` during `processing`. MDN: `aria-busy="true"` tells
194	  assistive technology "to wait until the modifications or changes are complete before exposing
195	  the content". Therefore the status and alert regions are placed **outside** the busy subtree,
196	  or they would be held back.
197	- A polite `role="status"` region, outside the busy subtree and present from the start (empty),
198	  receives "Procesando pago…" once when the attempt starts and is emptied when it ends.
199	- On rejection: `aria-busy` is removed first, then the rejection message is rendered in a
200	  `role="alert"` region next to "Pagar" (outside the busy subtree); focus stays on "Pagar"
201	  (US-03-Q-09). The message is removed when a new attempt starts.
202	- On approval: focus moves to the confirmation heading and the title changes (US-03-AC-16).
203	- No animation is needed; if a spinner is added, it respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.
204	
205	**How "no real card data" is guaranteed (D1) and how a reviewer verifies it**
206	
207	Guarantees by construction:
208	
209	- The summary and confirmation contain exactly three form controls: the terms checkbox and the two
210	  outcome radios. No `input`, `select` or `textarea` exists for card, expiry, security code, bank
211	  or any personal data, and no element carries an `autocomplete` token starting with `cc-` (which
212	  would invite the browser to autofill a saved real card).
213	- `PaymentGateway`'s request type has no field that could hold card data; `SimulatedPaymentGateway`
214	  injects no `HttpClient`.
215	- No payment SDK or third-party script is added: `frontend/package.json` dependencies are
216	  unchanged by US-03.
217	- The proxy and Strapi are unchanged except for the terms read path (spec §7.4).
218	
219	Checks:
220	
221	- Component test (`summary-page.spec.ts`, US-03-AC-15): the page's `input`, `select` and
222	  `textarea` elements are exactly one checkbox and two radios; no `autocomplete^="cc-"`.
223	- Unit test (`simulated-payment-gateway.spec.ts`): with `provideHttpClientTesting()`,
224	  `HttpTestingController.verify()` passes after an approved and a rejected attempt; the result
225	  arrives at 1500 ms and not before; a second `pay` during an attempt starts no timer; abort
226	  rejects and starts nothing.
227	- E2E (`full-flow-co`, US-03-AC-15, AC-19): `page.on('request')` records **zero** requests between
228	  the activation of "Pagar" and the confirmation heading.
229	- Review: `grep -rniE "cc-(number|exp|csc)|card|tarjeta|cvv|cvc|iban" frontend/src` returns no
230	  match outside copy that says no charge is made; `git diff main -- frontend/package.json` shows no
231	  new dependency.
232	
233	### Consequences
234	
235	- Good, because both outcomes are reachable deterministically, by users and tests, with the same
236	  build and no hidden switch (D2).
237	- Good, because no card data can be entered: there is nowhere to type it, and no browser autofill
238	  target exists (D1).
239	- Good, because nothing is sent: the payment adds no request, permission, route or backend code
240	  (D5, D8).
241	- Good, because the story's "Given the simulated payment fails, When I click pay" maps directly to
242	  "choose Pago rechazado, then Pagar".
243	- Good, because a real gateway replaces one provider and one request type; the page's states and
244	  the clearing rules stay (D9).
245	- Bad, because a test control sits in front of every user: a real checkout never lets the buyer
246	  choose the outcome — mitigation: the legend says "Simulación de pago (no se realiza ningún
247	  cobro)", the confirmation repeats that no real charge was made, and the group disappears when a
248	  real gateway is integrated.
249	- Bad, because the fixed 1.5 s adds 1.5 s to every payment attempt in the e2e runs — mitigation:
250	  accepted; it is the time AC-15 checks, and the planned e2e files make only a few attempts.
251	- Bad, because quote numbers can repeat across sessions — mitigation: they are fictitious, never
252	  stored or looked up, and only shown once.
253	- Neutral: the abstract-class boundary is a small indirection for a single implementation; it is
254	  the seam the spec asked for (D9) and the place tests substitute.
255	
256	### Strongest argument against
257	
258	Option B, the mock gateway screen, is what the assessment literally names ("a confirmation screen
259	or a mock gateway"), and it keeps the product honest: the summary looks like a real checkout, and
260	the decision about the outcome is made where a real gateway would make it, on a separate screen
261	after "Pagar". Option A instead puts a test harness control ("Pago aprobado / Pago rechazado")
262	on the production summary, in front of every user, next to the button that is supposed to take
263	their money. An evaluator may read that as leaking test concerns into the user interface, and a
264	user may wonder why they are asked whether they want their payment to fail.
265	
266	**Why we accept it:** B costs a new route and guard (an ADR-0001 note) or a modal dialog with its
267	own focus trap, splits the double-submit lock across two screens, and moves the choice after the
268	click, so the story's "Given … fails, When I click pay" no longer reads as written (US-03-Q-01).
269	Both options are equally simulated and equally deterministic; A gets there with one native radio
270	group, no new route and one fewer step for keyboard users. The legend and the confirmation notice
271	make the simulation explicit, and the gateway boundary means the control disappears with a real
272	integration. The human accepted this direction at HC1.
273	
274	### Confirmation
275	
276	- Unit: `simulated-payment-gateway.spec.ts` (fake timers: approved and rejected at 1500 ms, not
277	  at 1499 ms; in-flight rejection; abort; no HTTP), `quote-number.spec.ts` (every US-03-AC-10 row
278	  with a pinned `CLOCK` and a fixed `RANDOM_DIGITS`; the default source's range),
279	  `quote-store-clear.spec.ts` (entry and in-memory state deleted by `clearQuote()`; nothing
280	  removed on rejection).
281	- Component: `summary-page.spec.ts`: default "Pago aprobado"; exactly three form controls; three
282	  activations within 200 ms start one attempt (US-03-AC-09); during processing every action is
283	  unavailable and "Pagar" keeps focus; `aria-busy` and the status region outside it; rejection in
284	  `role="alert"`, state kept, focus on "Pagar"; on approval the store is cleared before the
285	  confirmation renders, focus and title per US-03-AC-16.
286	- E2E: `full-flow-co` (approved path, zero requests during payment, storage cleared, reload and
287	  back lead to an empty step 1, double activation) and `summary-payment-cl` (rejected, then
288	  approved).
289	- Review checklist: "Disabled pay button: its state is perceivable"; the grep and dependency checks
290	  above; `sessionStorage` referenced only in `QuoteStore`; no `@defer` around the confirmation.
291	
292	## Pros and Cons of the Options
293	
294	### A. Visible outcome choice on the summary (chosen)
295	
296	- Good, because it is deterministic for both outcomes with the same build, and discoverable by
297	  testers and evaluators without documentation (D2).
298	- Good, because it asks for no card or personal data (D1) and sends nothing (D5).
299	- Good, because it needs no route, guard, dialog or dependency (D8).
300	- Good, because the outcome is set before the click, as the story's scenario is written.
301	- Bad, because a simulation control is visible to every user of the production build.
302	- Bad, because it adds a control to the keyboard path (one more Tab stop, US-03-AC-16).
303	
304	### B. Mock gateway screen
305	
306	- Good, because it is the assessment's own example and mirrors a real hosted-gateway redirect.
307	- Good, because the summary stays free of simulation controls.
308	- Good, because the outcome is still deterministic and testable with the same build.
309	- Bad, because a route needs a guard and an ADR-0001 note (US-03-Q-06 kept the confirmation on
310	  `/resumen` to avoid this); a dialog needs a focus trap, `Escape` handling and focus return.
311	- Bad, because the double-submit lock spans "Pagar" and the gateway screen, and "cancel" on the
312	  gateway is a third outcome to specify.
313	- Bad, because the outcome is chosen after "Pagar", so AC-03, AC-04 and AC-15 would be rewritten.
314	
315	### C. Deterministic rule on the input (magic values)
316	
317	- Good, because there is no extra UI; real gateway sandboxes work this way.
318	- Good, because it is deterministic.
319	- Bad, because it is hidden: production code contains behaviour only testers know about, which is
320	  test-only logic in the shipped build.
321	- Bad, because it reads personal data (document number or plate) in the payment path, and the
322	  key may not exist: editors can remove or rename fields (US-01; ADR-0001).
323	- Bad, because the CL e2e must use different, "magic" step 1 data instead of the shared fictitious
324	  seed values; the URL-parameter variant is equally hidden and can be shared by link.
325	
326	### D. Random outcome
327	
328	- Good, because there is no extra UI and it feels like a real, occasionally failing gateway.
329	- Bad, because it is not deterministic (against BR-08): a user or a demo fails at random, and the
330	  e2e must patch `Math.random` or the crypto source through an init script, a test-only
331	  manipulation of the build.
332	- Bad, because a flaky outcome makes manual QA at HC3 non-repeatable.
333	
334	### E. Fictitious test card form
335	
336	- Good, because it looks like a real checkout and exercises form validation.
337	- Bad, because it invites real card entry: browsers offer to autofill saved real cards into fields
338	  marked as card fields, and nothing stops a person from typing their own card (against D1, the
339	  assessment's "do not use real card data").
340	- Bad, because card-shaped data would sit in the page's memory and in any error log by accident,
341	  which a real system would handle under PCI DSS; avoiding it entirely is simpler and safer.
342	- Bad, because it adds fields, validation and copy for no requirement.
343	
344	## Spec impact
345	
346	None that changes an AC. The approved spec v0.1 describes this option (US-03-Q-01, AC-15, §8.1).
347	Precisions this ADR adds, for the test-engineer and the developers:
348	
349	- The spec's `payment.spec.ts` is named `simulated-payment-gateway.spec.ts` (§11 left the name to
350	  this ADR).
351	- "Disabled" during processing (US-03-BR-05, AC-03) is `aria-disabled="true"` on "Pagar" so it
352	  keeps focus (consistent with US-03-Q-17); Playwright's `toBeDisabled()` accepts `aria-disabled`
353	  (verified, `playwright/types/test.d.ts` 1.65.1: "Element is disabled if it has 'disabled'
354	  attribute or is disabled via 'aria-disabled'").
355	- US-03-AC-15's "1.5 seconds after the activation" is measured from the test process with a
356	  tolerance, because the page clock is pinned.
357	
358	## More Information
359	
360	- Verified on 2026-11-21 in the installed packages: `@angular/core` 22.3.0, `vitest` 5.1.1,
361	  `@playwright/test` and `playwright-core` 1.65.1 (versions read from each `package.json` under
362	  `frontend/node_modules`):
363	  - `page.clock.setFixedTime` keeps timers running; `page.clock.install` fakes timers until
364	    `runFor`/`fastForward` (`playwright-core/types/types.d.ts`, `Clock` interface).
365	  - `toBeDisabled()` covers `aria-disabled` (`playwright/types/test.d.ts`).
366	  - `vi.useFakeTimers` and `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync` (`vitest/dist/index.d.ts`, lines 437 and
367	    473).
368	  - `CLOCK` is `InjectionToken<() => Date>` in `frontend/src/app/core/clock.ts`.
369	  - The nginx allow-list (`frontend/nginx/default.conf.template`) answers `405` to any method other
370	    than `GET`/`HEAD`, which is why the backend mock endpoint is excluded.
371	- MDN, `Crypto.getRandomValues()`
372	  (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Crypto/getRandomValues, read 2026-11-21):
373	  fills the array with cryptographically random numbers; usable from an insecure context.
374	- MDN, `aria-busy`
375	  (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-busy,
376	  read 2026-11-21).
377	- MDN, HTML `disabled` attribute
378	  (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Attributes/disabled, read
379	  2026-11-21): "disabled controls cannot receive focus".
380	- Related ADRs: ADR-0001 (route and guards unchanged), ADR-0002 and ADR-0005 (read-only access;
381	  why a backend mock is excluded), ADR-0003 (clearing rules), ADR-0007 (price shown, not passed to
382	  the gateway).
383	- Revisit when: a real payment provider is integrated (replace `SimulatedPaymentGateway`, remove
384	  the outcome choice, use the provider's hosted fields so card data never touches this app), or
385	  the product needs a stored quote or receipt (needs a server; out of scope).
386
